newsitem.title: UK: British serial-killer trial exposed child-crisis.
newsitem.headline: British serial-killer trial exposed child-crisis.

text.p: Hundreds of children meant to be in the care of British welfare services have simply disappeared, a report published on Friday said.
It said this emerged at the trial of serial killer Rosemary West sentenced to life imprisonment last year for the sexual torture and murder of 10 young women.
Social workers believe that up to 13,000 children go missing every year from children's homes in Britain and they want a national register set up to help trace them.
A confidential report leaked to BBC radio said welfare services had lost track of records of one in six of the children who were supposed to be in their care.
The report was commissioned by the council in the county of Gloucestershire, where Rosemary West and her husband Fred carried out their grisly crimes.
West's husband was also charged with 12 murders but committed suicide before he could face trial.
The investigation into their killing career found that they had preyed on vulnerable young women and that several of their victims came from children's homes.
Police trying to trace other potential victims found that local institutions had simply lost track of many of the children and young adults in their care.
